title: Doing Something So That Something Happens

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *para que* + the subjunctive from B1 Unit 4, and the imperfect subjunctive after a past verb from B1 Unit 38. They say what someone did so that something else would happen, which is how the Zapatista story explains its aims. The subjects are different; if the subject is the same, use *para* + infinitive (A2 Unit 30).

sections.title: Present and past purpose
rows: Se reúnen para que todos puedan opinar.
present: main verb in the present, subjunctive in the present (they meet so that everyone can speak)
Crearon escuelas para que los niños aprendieran en su lengua.
past: main verb in the past, imperfect subjunctive (they created schools so that the children would learn in their language)
Hablaron con la prensa para que el mundo conociera su situación.
past: *conociera* after *hablaron* (they spoke to the press so that the world would know their situation)
same subject: *para* + infinitive (they fought to defend their lands)

items.spanish: Los zapatistas se organizaron para que el Gobierno los escuchara.
items.english: The Zapatistas organised so that the government would listen to them.

items.spanish: Según el EZLN, crearon los Caracoles para que las comunidades decidieran por sí mismas.
items.english: According to the EZLN, they created the Caracoles so that the communities would decide for themselves.

items.spanish: Las comunidades se reúnen para que todos puedan hablar.
items.english: The communities meet so that everyone can speak.

items.spanish: Escribieron comunicados para que otras personas conocieran su situación.
items.english: They wrote communiqués so that other people would know their situation.

sections.content: After *para que* the verb is always in the subjunctive: present (*puedan*) when the main verb is in the present, imperfect (*decidieran*, *conociera*) when the main verb is in the past. Never the indicative: not *para que decidían*.
